workPackageTitle: Pin Godot/.NET versions, solution/project skeleton, repository layout, editor/analyzer settings
notes: Entries are added before implementation and are never renumbered (docs/technical/91 § Verification registry).
The structural validator for this file is owned by TASK-FND-009-002; until it lands, the shape here is the FND-001 integration owner's declaration of the required fields listed in doc 91.
Selectors are repository scripts and commands because the pure NUnit harness does not exist until TASK-FND-003-001. TASK-FND-009-001 replaces the architecture selector with an architecture test.

VER-FND-001-012 and VER-FND-001-013 use build/verify-godot.sh rather than the bare godot commands: a headless Godot launch exits 0 even when the boot script fails to load, so the exit code alone is not a gate. The script also asserts the stable startup line and the absence of engine ERROR lines.

The 'platforms' list records the platforms an entry has actually been executed on, not the platforms its subject is intended to support. Every entry in this file is linux-x64 only. VER-FND-001-001 and VER-FND-001-002 previously also listed windows-x64 and osx-arm64; that was wrong and is corrected here. Nothing in this repository has ever run either of them on Windows or macOS: build/bootstrap-linux.sh is the only provisioner, it provisions linux-x64, and build/toolchain.json's godot.unpinned_platform_policy records the same gap for the Godot pins. Restoring windows-x64 or osx-arm64 to any entry requires an actual run on that platform, which needs a CI runner for it - FND-005 owns the CI suite. Cross-platform restore and warning-free compilation are still intended properties of the pinned toolchain; they are simply unverified, and an unverified intention does not belong in a coverage field.

entries.summary: A clean checkout restores the exact locked NuGet graph and fails if any lock file would change. Executed on linux-x64 only; windows-x64 and osx-arm64 are PENDING and have never been run, so they are not listed under platforms.

The whole solution compiles from a clean checkout with zero warnings and zero errors under the pinned SDK, target framework, and language version. Executed on linux-x64 only; windows-x64 and osx-arm64 are PENDING and have never been run, so they are not listed under platforms.
The solution contains exactly the nine accepted projects at exactly the accepted repository paths, and every prescribed top-level ownership directory exists.

Project references match the accepted project boundary exactly, no pure project references Godot or MechaMiner.Game, and game/ is the only Godot-referencing project. The source scan for the Godot namespace is read twice, by build/verify-architecture.sh § 6 and by ProjectGraph.NamesGodotNamespace, against one shared control list: the six spellings C# offers for naming a namespace, plus three probes that put a decoy and a reference on the SAME line - a quote held in a char literal, a // inside a string, and a URL inside a string. The same-line probes exist because the six spellings each occupied a line of their own, which is why both readers reported green while the single line 'char q = (quote); Godot.GD.Print(y);' evaded the real scan: the quote inside the char literal opened a string state neither stripper knew how to leave, so the reference after it was blanked. NAMED GAP, not covered by either reader: C# permits Unicode escapes inside identifiers, so an import or a qualifier that spells one letter of Godot as an escape is valid C# that the compiler resolves to Godot and that neither reader sees. Closing it needs identifier position told apart from literal position, which is a parser rather than a text scan; an analyzer over the syntax tree is the mechanism that would do it, and no text scan in this gate can. The control set therefore reports the forms it covers rather than claiming all of them.

No GDScript source file exists outside documentation, tracked or untracked, so no runtime logic can use a second language. The candidate set is tracked plus untracked-but-not-ignored, and a failed enumeration fails the gate rather than emptying it. Both halves are stated because neither used to hold: the check consulted only tracked paths, so an untracked .gd file passed, and it discarded git's exit status with a trailing '|| true', so under a broken or absent git an empty result took the pass branch and this hard prohibition was silently unenforceable. Two negative controls run in the same invocation: an untracked .gd fixture must be reported as a violation, and the same probe under a broken GIT_DIR must report that it could not tell rather than reporting a clean tree.
Nullable reference checking is enabled repository-wide and a nullable violation is a build error, not a warning.
Built-in .NET analyzers are enabled and an analyzer violation fails the build.
The .editorconfig naming policy is enforced during build and a naming violation fails the build.
The C# language version is pinned, so a language feature newer than the pin fails the build instead of silently compiling.
Unsafe code is disabled by default and an unsafe block fails the build.
Deterministic build is enabled: two independent clean builds of the same source produce byte-identical assemblies.
A headless Godot import of game/ completes with exit code 0 from a clean checkout with no import cache.
A headless launch of the empty boot scene reaches the composition root, prints its stable startup line, and exits 0 with the Mobile renderer configured.
